content.text: The insurance clause is present and meets every element of our preferred position, so no redline is needed.

input.quote: 18.1 Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense throughout the term and for one year afterward, commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000.
input.rationale: Section 18 imposes insurance obligations on Vendor that match or exceed our preferred position: CGL at USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, professional E&O at USD 2M, cyber and privacy liability at USD 5M (Vendor hosts and processes Customer Data), and workers' compensation as required by law, all maintained at Vendor's expense through the term plus one year. Section 18.2 adds certificates of insurance and evidence of coverage on request, primary-coverage language, advance notice of cancellation or material reduction, and confirms that insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities (consistent with the Section 21 cap and Excluded Claims). Employer's liability of USD 1M is an extra protection beyond the playbook ask. The obligations run against the counterparty and benefit us, so nothing to flag; additional-insured status is not a playbook requirement and the non-limitation language adequately preserves our remedies.
